semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers z and N, if z is less than N, then z is less than or equal to N minus 1.

variables.name: z
variables.role: an arbitrary integer used in the inequality

variables.name: N
variables.role: an arbitrary integer compared against z

payload.statement_nl: For every integers z and N, if z < N, then z ≤ N - 1.

result_payload.proof_nl: Let z and N be integers, and assume z < N. Then N - z is an integer and N - z > 0, so N - z is a positive integer. Hence N - z >= 1. Rearranging gives z <= N - 1. Therefore, if z < N, then z <= N - 1.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the integer difference N-z: it is a positive integer, hence at least 1, which rearranges to z <= N-1.

used_external_facts: A positive integer is at least 1.
Basic closure of integers under subtraction.
